## Role in the pipeline

| | |
|---|---|
| **Thesis section** | 3.2 Firm data and analysis sample (panel construction) |
| **Input** | `Compustat North America Data.csv`, `Compustat Global Data Start 1988.csv`, `exchange_rates.csv` |
| **Output** | `compustat_panel.rds` (firm-year panel, 1988-2024) |
| **Previous / next file** | `01_alliance_data.qmd` / `03_linking_and_distance.qmd` |

This file builds the firm-year panel from Compustat North America and
Compustat Global: it stacks the two sources, defines revenue growth and the
control variables, fills the historical SIC code (`sich`) and converts
assets and revenue to USD.

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("00_config.R")
```

## 1. Read the raw files

`colClasses` keeps identifiers and SIC codes as text, so that they are not
altered (e.g. leading zeros).

```{r}
#| label: read
na <- fread(file.path(path, "Compustat North America Data.csv"),
            colClasses = list(character = c("gvkey", "sich", "naicsh", "cusip")),
            na.strings = c("", "NA"))
gl <- fread(file.path(path, "Compustat Global Data Start 1988.csv"),
            colClasses = list(character = c("gvkey", "sich", "naicsh", "isin", "sedol")),
            na.strings = c("", "NA"))

dim(na)   # 607,056 rows, 17 columns
dim(gl)   # 832,840 rows, 19 columns

knitr::kable(na[, .N, by = indfmt], caption = "North America: INDL vs. FS duplicates")
```

## 2. Clean both sources

```{r}
#| label: clean
# -- North America --
na <- na[indfmt == "INDL"]                 # drops financial-services duplicates
na <- na[fyear >= 1988 & fyear <= 2024]    # same window as Global (starts 1988)
na <- na[!(is.na(at) & is.na(lt) & is.na(revt) & is.na(sale) & is.na(ni))]   # empty rows

# -- Global -- (the INDL/FS duplicates do not exist in this download)
gl <- gl[fyear >= 1988 & fyear <= 2024]
gl <- gl[!(is.na(at) & is.na(lt) & is.na(revt) & is.na(sale) & is.na(nicon))]

c(north_america = nrow(na), global = nrow(gl))

# harmonise the two sources
setnames(na, "ni", "nicon")
na[, `:=`(source = "NA", country = fic, isin = NA_character_,
          sedol = NA_character_, cusip6 = substr(cusip, 1, 6))]
gl[, `:=`(source = "Global", country = loc,
          cusip = NA_character_, cusip6 = NA_character_)]
```

## 3. One observation per firm-year, stack the sources

Within each source only one record per firm-year is kept (the one with the
highest revenue), and North America records that also exist in Global are
dropped.

```{r}
#| label: stack
dedup <- function(d) {
  setorder(d, gvkey, fyear, -revt, na.last = TRUE)
  unique(d, by = c("gvkey", "fyear"))
}
na <- dedup(na)
gl <- dedup(gl)

na <- na[!gl, on = .(gvkey, fyear)]   # keep NA rows that are not in Global

cols <- c("gvkey", "fyear", "conm", "source", "country", "fic", "cusip", "cusip6",
          "isin", "sedol", "curcd", "costat", "at", "lt", "revt", "sale",
          "nicon", "sich", "naicsh")

panel <- rbind(na[, ..cols], gl[, ..cols])
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(panel, by = c("gvkey", "fyear")))   # every firm-year only once
dim(panel)   # about 1.12 million firm-years
```

## 4. Revenue growth (raw)

One-year growth is only defined if the previous year exists without a gap,
the currency did not change, and the previous revenue is positive.
The forward growth rates of the dependent variable (t to t+3, t to t+1)
are built from these revenues in `04_analysis_sample.qmd`.

```{r}
#| label: growth
setorder(panel, gvkey, fyear)

panel[, `:=`(revt_lag  = shift(revt),
             fyear_lag = shift(fyear),
             curcd_lag = shift(curcd)), by = gvkey]

panel[, growth := fifelse(fyear_lag == fyear - 1 & curcd_lag == curcd & revt_lag > 0,
                          (revt - revt_lag) / revt_lag, NA_real_)]

# Why growth is missing (first year of firm, gap, currency switch, zero revenue)
knitr::kable(
  panel[is.na(growth), .(
    first_year_of_firm = sum(is.na(fyear_lag)),
    gap_in_series      = sum(!is.na(fyear_lag) & fyear_lag != fyear - 1),
    currency_change    = sum(!is.na(fyear_lag) & fyear_lag == fyear - 1 & curcd_lag != curcd, na.rm = TRUE),
    revenue_zero       = sum(!is.na(fyear_lag) & fyear_lag == fyear - 1 & revt_lag <= 0, na.rm = TRUE))],
  caption = "Firm-years without a one-year growth rate")

# The raw distribution has absurd extremes -> reason for winsorising later
quantile(panel$growth, c(0, 0.01, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.99, 1), na.rm = TRUE)

# Sanity check on a known firm
panel[conm %like% "APPLE INC", .(fyear, revt, growth = round(growth, 3))][fyear %in% 2015:2020]
```

## 5. Control variables (raw)

Past growth is the one-year growth of the *previous* year (t-2 to t-1);
all other controls are measured in year t.

```{r}
#| label: controls
panel[, `:=`(roa         = fifelse(at > 0, nicon / at, NA_real_),
             leverage    = fifelse(at > 0, lt / at,    NA_real_),
             ln_at_local = fifelse(at > 0, log(pmax(at, 1e-9)), NA_real_))]

panel[, `:=`(roa_l1      = fifelse(fyear_lag == fyear - 1, shift(roa),      NA_real_),
             leverage_l1 = fifelse(fyear_lag == fyear - 1, shift(leverage), NA_real_),
             growth_l1   = fifelse(fyear_lag == fyear - 1, shift(growth),   NA_real_)),
      by = gvkey]

# Firm age is NOT used in the models (collinear with firm and year FE, thesis 3.3.4)
panel[, age := fyear - min(fyear), by = gvkey]
```

## 6. Historical SIC code

`sich` is missing for 13.5% of firm-years. Firms rarely change industry, so
gaps are filled from the same firm's nearest earlier year, otherwise the
nearest later year. Firms without any `sich` stay missing and drop out of
the sample (2.8% of firm-years). The header SIC is deliberately not used,
because it reflects today's industry (Kahle & Walkling, 1996).

```{r}
#| label: sic
setorder(panel, gvkey, fyear)
panel[, sich_n := as.integer(as.character(sich))]
panel[, sich_fill_n := nafill(nafill(sich_n, "locf"), "nocb"), by = gvkey]
panel[, sic_origin := fcase(!is.na(sich_n),      "historical",
                            !is.na(sich_fill_n), "filled",
                            default = NA_character_)]
panel[, sich_fill := fifelse(is.na(sich_fill_n), NA_character_,
                             sprintf("%04d", sich_fill_n))]
panel[, sic2 := substr(sich_fill, 1, 2)]
panel[, financial := (sich_fill_n %/% 100) %between% c(60, 69)]
panel[, c("sich_n", "sich_fill_n") := NULL]

knitr::kable(panel[, .N, by = sic_origin][, share := round(N / sum(N), 3)],
             caption = "Origin of the SIC code")
```

## 7. Currency conversion to USD

Assets are a balance-sheet figure and use the year-end rate; revenue accrues
over the year and uses the annual average rate. The rates are calendar-year
rates, whereas `fyear` does not always end in December.

```{r}
#| label: fx
fx <- fread(file.path(path, "exchange_rates.csv"))
fx[, year := year(as.Date(datadate))]
setorder(fx, curd, datadate)

fx_end <- fx[!is.na(exratd_tousd), .SD[.N], by = .(curd, year), .SDcols = "exratd_tousd"]
setnames(fx_end, "exratd_tousd", "fx_end")
fx_avg <- fx[!is.na(exratd_tousd), .(fx_avg = mean(exratd_tousd)), by = .(curd, year)]

panel[fx_end, on = .(curcd = curd, fyear = year), fx_end := i.fx_end]
panel[fx_avg, on = .(curcd = curd, fyear = year), fx_avg := i.fx_avg]
panel[curcd == "USD", `:=`(fx_end = 1, fx_avg = 1)]

panel[, `:=`(at_usd = at * fx_end, revt_usd = revt * fx_avg)]
panel[, ln_at_usd := fifelse(at_usd > 0, log(at_usd), NA_real_)]
setorder(panel, gvkey, fyear)
panel[, revt_usd_lag := fifelse(fyear_lag == fyear - 1, shift(revt_usd), NA_real_), by = gvkey]

knitr::kable(panel[, .(share_missing_fx = round(mean(is.na(fx_end)), 3)), by = source],
             caption = "Firm-years without an exchange rate")
```

## 8. Save

```{r}
#| label: save
saveRDS(panel, file.path(path, "compustat_panel.rds"))
```
